source_evidence.behavior: A 10,000-unit purchase receipt plus a 2,000-unit positive-quantity Out adjustment is expected to leave 8,000 balance in InventoryOverview; verifies signed direction handling on that path.
Test fixture and dashboard call exist; inspected test class contains no owner-dashboard low-stock comparison for Out movement.

callable_review.reasoning: The author receipt correctly observes the raw sum and minimum>0 rule, but its phrase “Same test the inventory screen uses” is incomplete/contradicted: the dashboard raw balance sum differs from `InventoryRules.StockBalanceMilliUnits` and `GetInventoryOverviewAsync`, which sign Out quantities. Since RecordWasteHandler stores positive quantity with Direction=Out, after 10,000 In and 2,000 Out the dashboard computes 12,000 while the inventory overview computes 8,000. For a positive threshold between those figures, inventory overview can report low stock while owner dashboard suppresses the warning. This affects stock-position/low-stock guidance, not a direct cash posting or priced stock-value calculation in this method.
counterevidence_and_limits: Dashboard intentionally suppresses low-stock alerts when MinimumMilliUnits is zero, even if balance is negative; this is source explicit and may be desired policy.
The dashboard only displays a low-stock list/count; it does not calculate stock valuation here. The direct effect is divergent alert balance, not direct posted accounting movement.

Existing InventoryOverview test proves the intended signed behavior for a positive Out count adjustment, but does not assert dashboard behavior for the same fixture. No test executed and no live database observed.
The source receipt itself references existing FIN013. Preserve/extend that finding; no duplicate finding is recommended.
